chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When a man is narrating a hadith and a sneezer sneezes, he is a witness to the truth.'

key_terms.حَدِيث: A religious narration or tradition, typically from the Prophet or Imams.
key_terms.شَاهِدُ حَقٍّ: A witness to the truth; indicating confirmation or authenticity.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of sneezing during the recitation of a hadith in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarly tradition, this hadith from Al-Kafi interprets the sneeze as a divine sign (isharah) confirming the truthfulness of the narrator, reflecting the belief that Allah assists the truth. It underscores the spiritual etiquette of the listener, where a natural bodily reaction is elevated to a witness of authenticity, reinforcing the reliability of transmitted knowledge. This concept is often linked to the broader Islamic practice of responding to sneezes with 'Yarhamuk Allah,' here specifically applied to the context of religious discourse.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘When the man was narrating with a Hadeeth, so a sneezer sneezes, so it is a testimony of truthfulness’.
en.sarwar: 25. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
‘‘The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘If a man is speaking about something and someone sneezes, this is evidence of the truth.’”
